chunks: 3 - Muhammad b. al-Hasan (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us. He said: Al-'Abbas b. Ma'ruf narrated to us from Muhammad b. Sinan from Talha b. Zayd from al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad from his father from his forefathers (peace be upon them). He said:
Whoever says the takbir to Allah, Blessed and Exalted, one hundred times in the evening, it is as though he freed one hundred persons.

key_terms.نَسَمَة: Nasama: a person or soul, referring to freeing enslaved people

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for saying takbir 100 times in the evening according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated through a chain reaching Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS), highlights the immense reward of saying the takbir (Allahu Akbar) one hundred times in the evening. The reward is compared to freeing one hundred slaves, which in the prophetic tradition represents one of the highest forms of charitable acts. This teaching was delivered in a Ramadan assembly in 367 AH.

en.bilal-muhammad: Muhammad b. al-Hasan (ra) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us. He said: Al-`Abbas b. Ma`ruf narrated to us from Muhammad b. Sinan from Talha b. Zayd from al-Sadiq Ja`far b. Muhammad from his father from his forefathers (as). He said:
Whoever extols Allah (takbir) one hundred times in the evening, it is as though he frees one hundred people.
